answered.title: How the father's death was changed
answered.answer: No murder. The father dies an ordinary death while young; the story's weight is the hole left in the kid's life and grief too large to understand.

answered.title: Camera and physics on the player
answered.answer: Physics owns what you see: the eye rides a simulated head filtered toward today's springs, body reactions are physical, with a small inertia dial on reversals, off by default. Aim and root stay as they are.

answered.title: Hunter's cornering and every entity's shape
answered.answer: The hunter corners by the hunting-animal law in a humanoid body. Every entity is humanoid in nature with its own unique uncanniness.

answered.title: Each kind's one trait
answered.answer: Hunter T1 only (greyhound cornering, head stays humanlike); sprinter T3 (galloping back flex); pack T4 (shared fixed rhythm); interceptor T2; crawler T4; stalker T2; charger T3. Lesser kinds take theirs when they get humanoid models.

answered.title: Lean, facing and climbs
answered.answer: The lean is both, tilt first. While sliding, the hunter faces you. The climb uses Overgrowth's grips, procedural, no clips (this settles clips versus procedure for climbs).

answered.title: First-person body picks
answered.answer: A shoulder sliver on the look-back, a loose fist at the top of the sprint swing, the leading leg shown in a slide.

answered.title: Arm swing
answered.answer: Both: a bigger swing at speed and the arms riding more of the torso's twist. Your eye is the bar.

answered.title: Arm numbers: keep or you pick
answered.answer: You pick: variants are shown side by side (the measured one beside two pushed toward your description) before any landing; your eye is the bar for the look, the research is how it is built.

answered.title: When a run is lost and when it is saved
answered.answer: Caught before the timer: lose all points. Survive the timer: overtime where the evil god always catches you and the good god always saves you, run counts as a success with points kept plus the overtime bonus. Being consumed happens only before the timer.

answered.title: Two currencies
answered.answer: Cash (spent at the PC on most things) and energy (spent in the meditation chair); the illicit site's rare trinkets cost a mix of both.

answered.title: Lost run still gives some global XP
answered.answer: A lost run gives crumbs of global XP compared with winning; energy comes from successful escapes and chests.

answered.title: Luck and the Park's length
answered.answer: No sealed pieces. Luck does not touch a Park's length; it acts on chests only (more often, better loot, several things at once).

answered.title: Park erosion start and name
answered.answer: Erosion starts 15 seconds after first entry, creeping about 3 m/s. The safe zones are called the Park.

answered.title: How the surge is limited
answered.answer: Diminishing returns replace per-source cooldowns; the base surge is limited; abilities raise the limits. Surge is earned by overtakes fused with near misses.

answered.title: Kid's base outfit
answered.answer: The kid starts in your own regular clothing, no buff. The father's hoodie is a late-game unlock. (Which of the three design sheets is not yet picked; see the open call.)

answered.title: Flashlight is not one of the six
answered.answer: You do not spawn with it; you find it in chests; it is unlocked early.

answered.title: Only one character is played
answered.answer: One playable character, made great: the kid. Other characters are set aside, not deleted.

answered.title: Father's things
answered.answer: Dad's watch is a trinket; his bomber a legendary jacket; his sunglasses a legendary accessory.

answered.title: No out-of-body moments in the dream
answered.answer: You said there should be none in the dreamzone, since you are already out of your body.

answered.title: Own sounds from scratch
answered.answer: No: use an open-source, high-quality synth or something beyond the native sound capabilities.

answered.title: Sprint peak
answered.answer: Top sprint speed about 10 m/s, earned by holding sprint and taking good lines, with the chasers scaled to match.

answered.title: Chaser counts and early runs
answered.answer: Count of chasers scales with base difficulty and story progression; the first few runs are forgiving.

answered.title: Lore depth
answered.answer: Surface play first; lore never forced, abundant for those who search, built on real research woven into a fictional frame.

answered.title: The dark one's name candidates
answered.answer: The four candidates were 'good for now'; the name stays open among them; the build uses a placeholder.

answered.title: The apartment and variety
answered.answer: Frozen. New structure goes into the hotel, school and hospital first.

answered.answer: Two more.
